source.author: stat
source.text: Cetera Graiorum curis armisque iacebat fessa cohors; alto castrorum ex aggere Arrastus lactificos tenui captabat corde tumultus, quamquam aeger senio, sed agit miseranda-potestas invigilare malis, illum aereus undique clamor Thebanique urunt sonitus, et amara lacessit tibia, tum nimio voces marcore superbae incertaeque faces et iam male pervigil ignis, sic ubi per fluctus uno ratis obruta somno conticuit, pacique maris secura iuventus mandavere animas: solus stat puppe magister pervigil inscriptaque deus qui navigat alno.
source.text_original: Cetera Graiorum curis armisque iacebat / fessa cohors; alto castrorum ex aggere Arrastus / lactificos tenui captabat corde tumultus, / quamquam aeger senio, sed agit miseranda-potestas / invigilare malis, illum aereus undique clamor / Thebanique urunt sonitus, et amara lacessit / tibia, tum nimio voces marcore superbae / incertaeque faces et iam male pervigil ignis, / sic ubi per fluctus uno ratis obruta somno / conticuit, pacique maris secura iuventus / mandavere animas: solus stat puppe magister / pervigil inscriptaque deus qui navigat alno.
source.text_english: The rest of the Greek host lay worn out by cares and arms; from the high mound of the camp Arrastus, though sick with old age, with a thin heart caught the joyful uproars, but wretched duty drives him to keep watch over evils. On every side the brazen din and Theban noises burn him, and the bitter flute assails him; then, with great languor, the proud and uncertain watchfires and the fire now badly kept awake. So, when a ship, buried in the waves, has fallen silent in one sleep, and the young men, trusting in the peace of the sea, have entrusted their lives: alone on the stern stands the watchful pilot, and the god who sails in the inscribed alder tree.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: te quoque Thessalicae, Nestor, rapit in freta puppis fama, Mycenaeis olim qui candida velis aequora et instantes mirabere mille magistros.
reuse.text_original: te quoque Thessalicae, Nestor, rapit in freta puppis / fama, Mycenaeis olim qui candida velis / aequora et instantes mirabere mille magistros.
reuse.text_english: Fame also carries you, Nestor, in the Thessalian sea of the ship, you who once would marvel at the bright waters with Mycenaean sails and a thousand masters pressing close.
